# `silk/schema/issue`

<!-- Generated by silk doc-reference. Do not edit by hand. -->

The problems a schema reports, and where in the value and the input they happened.

## When to use
Match on [`Issue`](#Issue) when a codec, a check, or a format reader rejects input. Read
[`SchemaError`](#SchemaError) from `silk.schema.json.SchemaJson.decode`, or [`SchemaErrors`](#SchemaErrors) from
`SchemaJson.decodeAll`, and show them with `silk.schema.report.SchemaReport`.

## Details
An `Issue` is a small copyable value: an [`IssueReason`](#IssueReason), one line of static text that names what
was expected, the kind of value found, and the [`Span`](#Span) of input bytes it is about when the
format knows it. A `SchemaError` adds the [`SchemaPath`](./schema-path.md#SchemaPath) from the root value to the part that
failed. Nothing copies the input: a report cuts the found value out of the input by its span.

Import as `Issue` with `import silk.schema.issue { Issue }`.

<a id="Issue"></a>

## `Issue`

```silk
pub struct Issue
```

One problem found while reading, writing, or checking a value.

### Details

`expected` is one line of static text that says what the schema wanted, such as `"a number"` or
`"an integer from 1 to 65535"`. `found` is the kind of value the input held, and `span` the
bytes of the input the problem is about, when the format knows them.

<a id="Issue.reason"></a>

### Field `reason`

```silk
pub reason: IssueReason
```

Why the value was rejected.

<a id="Issue.expected"></a>

### Field `expected`

```silk
pub expected: string<'static>
```

What the schema expected, as one line of text for a person.

<a id="Issue.found"></a>

### Field `found`

```silk
pub found: ValueKind
```

The kind of value the input held.

<a id="Issue.span"></a>

### Field `span`

```silk
pub span: Option<Span>
```

The bytes of the input the problem is about, if known.

<a id="SchemaError"></a>

## `SchemaError`

```silk
pub struct SchemaError
```

A rejected value: the problem, and the path from the root value to the part that failed.

### Details

`path` keeps its segments, so it renders with wire names for a person
(`SchemaPath.text`), as a JSON Pointer for a tool (`SchemaPath.pointer`), or with Silk names
(`SchemaPath.names`). It is empty when the root value itself failed.

<a id="SchemaError.path"></a>

### Field `path`

```silk
pub path: SchemaPath
```

The path from the root value to the part that failed, such as `settings.ports[2]`.

<a id="SchemaError.issue"></a>

### Field `issue`

```silk
pub issue: Issue
```

The problem.

<a id="SchemaErrors"></a>

## `SchemaErrors`

```silk
pub struct SchemaErrors
```

Every problem found while reading one value, in input order.

### Details

`silk.schema.json.SchemaJson.decodeAll` reports it. A part that fails is recorded and
skipped, and reading goes on with its next sibling, so one call lists every problem in the
input, up to [`MAX_PROBLEMS`](#MAX_PROBLEMS).

<a id="SchemaErrors.errors"></a>

### Field `errors`

```silk
pub errors: List<SchemaError>
```

The problems, never empty.

<a id="SchemaErrors.dropped"></a>

### Field `dropped`

```silk
pub dropped: usize
```

How many more problems were found after the first `MAX_PROBLEMS`.
